title: upgrade attention kernels: flashattentionv2 + fused ops + rotary/rope optimizations
author: Diego Morales
description:
Motivation: Reduce per-token latency and cost for medium- and long-context workloads by upgrading our attention kernels to FlashAttentionV2-style algorithms, adding a set of fused attention ops, and optimizing rotary/ROPE application to avoid extra memory copies. This PR replaces the legacy attention path for NVIDIA GPUs with a new codepath that selects FlashAttentionV2 (with fused softmax + dropout when applicable), introduces a fused qkv->attn->out kernel for common layer patterns, and optimizes rotary/ROPE math to operate in-place on GPU registers where possible.

Summary of changes: single continuous description string includes implementation notes, tests, and rollout plan.

Implementation: - Add flash_attn_v2.cu: implementation adapted from reference FlashAttentionV2 ideas (memory-efficient tiling, block-aligned softmax) and integrated with our kernel launching conventions. - Add fused_ops.cu: fused qkv projection + attention kernel for cases where model layout and dtype allow kernel fusion (FP16/TF32 with sequences > 128). - Add rope.cu: in-place rotary implementation with vectorized math path and fallback for legacy tensors. - Integrate kernel selection in runtime/attention/selector.cpp: runtime picks (1) fused qkv-attn if model/shape/flags match, (2) FlashAttentionV2 path if GPU and sequence length benefit, (3) fallback to legacy aten-based attention. - Add scheduler hints in runner/scheduler.rs to expose preferred kernel and tile size to the request router for batch packing heuristics. - Add new perf benchmarks and CI microbench tests under tests/perf to track latency/P50/P99 and throughput. - Docs: docs/perf/attn_kernels.md describing tradeoffs and recommended config options.

Benchmarks (summary from perf harness on p4d.24xlarge-like machines, mixed-batch profile): - Legacy path (main): 12.6 ms median token latency, 1.0 tokens/sec per GPU throughput baseline. - FlashAttentionV2 path: 8.1 ms median (-35% lat), 1.6 tokens/sec per GPU throughput (+60%). - Fused qkv-attn (longer sequences >1024): 6.5 ms median (-48% lat), 1.9 tokens/sec per GPU (+90%). - Memory footprint reduced ~18% for large context due to reduced KV temporary allocations. These numbers are for representative Llama-2-13B-like layer shapes; see tests/perf/bench-results/*.csv for full data.

Backward compatibility: The code respects model pinning and falls back to the legacy path automatically if a kernel is not compatible (e.g., mixed-precision inconsistencies, custom rotary scaling, or unsupported hardware). We added telemetry counters for kernel selection to help rollouts. No API surface change for users.

Testing: - Unit tests for numeric parity included (relative error thresholds) in tests/attn/unit_numeric.py. - End-to-end inference tests run in CI matrix across CUDA 11/12, NVIDIA driver versions used in our fleets. - Perf harness runs are gated behind nightly jobs; added a small CI microbench that runs on PR to catch regressions.

Rollout plan: 1) Merge to main behind a runtime feature flag (default enabled for canary fleet). 2) Canary deploy on ~5% of traffic (Dedicated + Hosted dev region) for 48h with rollback hooks. 3) Gradual ramp based on perf telemetry and 7-day error budget. 4) Full rollout if no regressions.

Related: ENG-4211 (attention kernel upgrade epic), ENG-4278 (rotary optimization follow-up).

Notes: Some synthetic unit tests initially flaked on float32 edge cases; resolved by tightened numerics and fallback path. The PR contains a small hotfix to scheduler packing logic to avoid pathological batching when fused kernels expect specific alignment.
